description.narrative:
Insatsen ”Georgia Agribusiness Competitiveness” är föreslagen av International Finance Corporation (IFC) i Europa och Asien till Sveriges ambassad i Tbilisi för samfinansiering. Insatsens mål är att stödja Georgiens lagstiftningsreformer för att uppfylla EU-kraven för livsmedelssäkerhet samt att stärka kapaciteten hos lokala aktörer inom jordbruket avseende modern livsmedelssäkerhet och standarder inom sektorn. Insatsen kommer att vara en del av ett större projekt ”Georgia Trade, Investment and Agri-competitiveness”, vilket samfinansieras av IFC och IFC Austria Trust Funds, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) och Multi Donor Trust Funds for Trade Facilitation. Insatsen kommer att utföras genom Världsbanksgruppens (inklusive IFC) gemensamma globala team "Finance, Competitiveness and Innovation practice". Insatsen kommer att genomföras av Världsbanksgruppen under perioden juli 2019 – december 2021. Den totala budgeten för projektet är 16 000 000 SEK, varav Sverige förväntas bidra med 5 700 000 SEK.
Det övergripande målet för projektet “Georgia Trade, Investment and Agri Competitiveness” är att främja hållbar tillväxt driven av privata sektorn i Georgien, genom att stödja den offentliga och privata sektorn med följande:
(i) Komponenten för ökad konkurrenskraft inom jordbruksnäring (Agri Competitiveness Component): Förbättra näringslivets efterlevnad av kraven i EU:s fördjupade frihandelsområde (DCFTA) genom att stödja tillämpningen av nya lagstiftningar inom livsmedelssäkerhet; introducera flexibel tillämpning av standarder för mindre, traditionella livsmedelsproducenter, förbättra biodlingsmetoder för utvalda honungsproducenter; öka kapaciteten hos inspektörer och laboratorier i enlighet med nya krav och med detta, öka honungsexporten till 750 000 USD (basvärdet är 21 200 USD) i december 2022, ett år efter komponentens avslut. (ii) Komponenten för investering (Investment Component): Attrahera och bevara investeringar till ett värde av minst 12 600 000 MUSD, två år efter komponentens avslut. (iii) Komponenten för handel (Trade Component): Effektivisera tullprocedurer genom att etablera ”National Trade Facilitation Committee”, i linje med avtalet för underlättande av handel (Trade Facilitation Agreement) samt effektivisera tullprocedurerna i linje med Världshandelsorganisationens avtal för tullvärdeberäkning.
Georgien är ett land med en liten inhemsk marknad. Landet är importberoende, fattigdomen är utspridd på landsbygden och inkomstfördelningen mellan stad och land är mycket ojämn. Georgien är i stort behov av att effektivisera möjligheterna för exporttillväxt och utveckla produktiviteten i jordbrukssektorn. Under 2017 utgjorde exporten 18 %, en relativt liten del av Georgiens BNP. Frihandelsavtalet med EU har avskaffat importtullar till EU- importerade jordbruksprodukter från Georgien och erbjuder lovande möjligheter för georgiska producenter - förutsatt att landets reglering och kontroll inom livsmedelssäkerheter är i linje med EU-standarder. En flexibel tillämpning av EU-standarder är särskilt viktigt för att säkerställa de små jordbruken, och de små och medelstora livsmedelsproducenternas intressen för framtida marknadssatsningar, både inom EU och internationellt.
Det svenska bidraget avser att stödja reformeringen av reglering för ökad konkurrenskraft inom jordbruksnäringen och med detta påskynda närmandet av Georgiens lagstiftning inom livsmedelssäkerhet till EU standarder; skydda georgiska traditionella producenter genom flexibel tillämpning av standarder; underlätta efterlevnaden av nya standarder och öppna nya marknader (projektpelare 1). Det svenska bidraget avser även att bidra till att utveckla kapaciteten och öka medvetandet för att föra vidare kunskap till den lokala jordbruksnäringen om modern livsmedelssäkerhet och standarder inom sektorn. (projektpelare 2).
Insatsen förväntas bidra till att närma det georgiska regelverket för livsmedelssäkerhet till EU standarder, öka honungsexport till EU och andra utvecklade marknader, och genom att tillämpa flexibelt genomförandet av EU kraven för livsmedelssäkerhet - skydda små lantbrukare och producenter på marknaden.

The intervention "Georgia Agribusiness Competitiveness", proposed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in Europe and Central Asia (member of the World Bank Group) to the Embassy of Sweden for co-funding, is aimed at supporting the regulatory reforms of Georgia's food safety legislation with the European Union (EU) requirements and capacity building of local agri-industry on modern food safety and industry standards. The intervention is one of the components of the overall project "Georgia Trade, Investment and Agri Competitiveness", which is co-funded by IFC's and IFC Austria Trust Funds, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and Multi Donor Trust Funds for Trade Facilitation. The intervention will be executed by the "Finance, Competitiveness and Innovation Practice" , a joint global practice of the World Bank Group (including IFC), during July 2019-December 2021. Total budget of the overall project amounts to 16 000 000 SEK out of which the expected Swedish contribution amounts to 5 700 000 SEK.
The overarching objective of the overall project "Georgia Trade, Investment and Agri Competitiveness" is to promote sustainable private sector-driven growth in Georgia by assisting the public and private sector with the following:
(i) Agri competitiveness component: Improve compliance of businesses with Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Agreement (DCFTA) requirements by supporting implementation of newly adopted food safety legislation; introducing flexible implementation of standards for small traditional producers; changing beekeeping practice of selected honey producers; increasing capacity of inspectors and laboratory on new requirements and, thus, increasing honey export to USD 750,000 (baseline is USD 21, 200) one year post-completion of the agri competitiveness component in December 2022; (ii) Investment component: Attract and retain investments generating at least 12 600 000 USD of investments two years post-completion of the investment component. (iii) Trade component: Streamline customs procedures through establishment of National Trade Facilitation Committee in line with Trade Facilitation Agreement and streamline customs valuation procedures in line with World Trade Organization (WTO) Customs Valuation Agreement.
Georgia, with its small domestic market, import dependency, widespread rural poverty, and rural-urban income inequality, needs high value-added, efficiency-seeking agri-sector development and export growth. In 2017, export made up a relatively small share of Georgia’s GDP, not more than 18%. The DCFTA, which removes import duties on EU agricultural imports from Georgia, offers promising opportunities for Georgian producers, provided that the country’s food safety regulations and controls are brought in line with EU standards. The flexible implementation of the EU standards is especially important when it comes to safeguarding Georgia’s smallholders and small and medium sized food producers interest in view of future market openings, both in the EU and internationally.
The Swedish contribution envisages to support regulatory reforms in the area of agribusiness competitiveness (project pillar 1) to expedite approximation of Georgia’s food safety legislation with EU requirements, protect Georgia’s traditional producers with the flexible implementation, facilitate compliance with new standards, and open new markets. It is also aimed towards capacity building and awareness creation to transmit knowledge of modern food safety requirements and industry standards to the local agri-industry.
The intervention is expected to contribute to increased EU approximation of the food safety regulations in Georgia, contribute to the increase of honey export to EU and other developed markets and to through flexible implementation of the food safety requirements - protect small producers and farmers on the market.

The overarching objective of the project: Georgia Trade, Investment and Agri Competitiveness is to promote sustainable private sector-driven growth in Georgia. The proposed intervention, targeting the Agri Competitiveness part of the project, is aimed at supporting the regulatory reforms of Georgia's food safety legislation with the European Union (EU) requirements and capacity building of local agri-industry on modern food safety and industry standards. The intervention aims to assist the public and private sector: improve compliance of businesses with the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Agreement (DCFTA) requirements by supporting implementation of newly adopted food safety legislation, introduction of flexible implementation of standards for small traditional producers, changing beekeeping practice of selected honey producers, increasing capacity of inspectors and laboratory on new requirements and, thus, growing exports of honey to USD 750,000 (baseline USD 21,200) one year post-completion of agri component (Dec 22); Through carrying out regulatory reforms in the area of agribusiness the intervention aims: (i) to expedite approximation of Georgia’s food safety legislation with EU requirements, protect Georgia’s traditional producers with the flexible implementation, facilitate compliance with new standards, and open new markets. (ii) to transmit knowledge of modern food safety requirements and industry standards to the local agri-industry.

The main accomplishments are specifically described below for each pillar.
Pillar 1: Regulatory Reform
The Project allocated certain efforts to support the local food safety system in approximation to the EU requirements, including options for flexible implementation of the food safety regulations. The Project closely collaborated with the Ministry of Environment Protection and Agriculture (MEPA) and the National Food Agency (NFA) on the relevant regulatory issues.
Support for EU Approximation
As a result of the Projects effective cooperation with MEPA and NFA aimed at facilitation of approximation of Georgian food safety legislation with the EU requirements, revisions to the following regulations have been approved by the Government of Georgia (GoG):
- Regulation #348, dated 14.07.2015 on implementation of the preventive and quarantine measures against animal transmissible diseases (revision applicable to the rules for preventive and quarantine measures against honeybee American foulbrood, honeybee parasite mite Tropilaelaps and colony pest Small Hive Beetle - Aethina tumida, dated 21.12.2022). Effective implementation of the preventive and control measures against the mentioned parasites is essential on the national level to safeguard further development of the local beekeeping sector and support queen bees export to the EU.
In addition, the following documents have been developed to facilitate effective implementation of existing regulatory requirements by the private sector and enhance inspection of the honey processors:
- Inspection check-list specifically designed for the honey processing sector (subject for approval by relevant authorities);
- 10 easy-to-read manuals for the food business-operators in accordance with the recently adopted Government regulations in the area of food safety, veterinary and plant protection;
- Publication on honeybee disease management and production of safe honey, based on the best international beekeeping practices and modern food safety principles.
Flexible Implementation
The Project organized workshops for MEPAs and NFAs representatives reviewing experience of different countries on flexible implementation of the EU harmonized food safety requirements and explaining how they could be implemented in less burdensome way letting small producers continue their operations following new requirements without compromising food safety. To assist MEPA in defining the scope for the relevant regulation, the Project also developed the following two reports: 1) Policy Brief on the Possibility of Application of Flexible / Simplified Approach in Georgian Food Safety Legislation and 2) Brief Analysis of Flexibility in EU Legislation.
Following these preparatory steps, the Project was involved in the initial development and further amendment of the Government Regulation #14 on the rules for disorganized production of food/feed (originally approved on 09.01.2020, revision approved on 01.04.2022). This regulation defines the operational definitions for unsystematic/disorganized production for the various agricultural sectors (e.g. not exceeding 10 bee hives for beekeeping, not exceeding 5 animals for cattle farming, etc.) and sets the basic requirements for those physical persons, who can benefit from flexible implementation of new food safety requirements while continuing their operations in less burdensome way, such as registration at the NFA and fulfilment of all guidelines imposed by the NFA in relation to the basic hygiene, animal health and plant protection.
Opening New Markets
In 2022 Georgian honey export reached the record indicator. 2022 export value equals to USD 1,2 million, showing 79% growth, compared to 2021. In volume terms, in 2022 Georgian honey export reached 258 tonnes, exceeding 2021 export data by almost 50%. 90% of total exported honey amount was designated for the EU market[1]. 38% of the total export volume (98.8 tonnes) is attributed to the Project beneficiaries.
Although overall export increase has not been directly linked to the export shipments implemented by the Project beneficiaries, it is apparent that the Projects activities facilitated this process and generated interest among the local beekeepers and exporters.
- In addition to the in-country activities, the Project supported participation of Georgian honey producers at international food fair in May 2022 in Italy. Green Hive Beekeepers Society, formed earlier by the Projects beneficiaries, presented five honey brands with a range of specialty honeys from Georgia
Pillar 2: Capacity Building and Awareness Creation
As a result of the technical assistance the following accomplishments have been achieved:
- 10 honey processors (who constructed new or rearranged existing honey processing facilities) were acknowledged compliant with the regulatory requirements and approved by the NFA.
- 1 honey processor set up in-house honey testing laboratory to establish efficient incoming honey control system.
- 4 operators are completing construction/remodeling of honey processing facilities. Apiary management and honey processing records have been maintained by most of the participating beekeepers. Record-keeping has been remaining a challenging issue among the local food producers, including beekeepers as well, mostly due to the lack of strict control over this requirement by the NFA.
- The Project has been constantly explaining importance of the record-keeping and offering assistance in completing the required records. 33 training sessions in modern beekeeping practices and food safety requirements have been delivered in 8 different locations to more than 350 participants, including beekeepers, laboratory representatives, NFAs personnel. Besides, in cooperation with IFC Moldova team, in 2022 the Project organized online discussion between Moldovan and Georgian beekeepers/honey producers to share Moldovas experience regarding the beekeeping sector development, penetration to the EU market and main challenges as well as solutions applied in this respect.
- 4 tutorials on management of American Foulbrood disease (major cause of honey contamination with antibiotics) were recorded and uploaded to YouTube: 1 honey producer was awarded the organic certificate for his apiary and processing facility. There is a potential interest from the consumers in relation to the organic products. Besides, the state program supporting promotion of bio production has been announced. The beneficiary honey processors whose facilities have already been approved by the NFA, started offering honey processing services to other beekeepers, thus in frequent cases indirectly contributing to local and export sales increase.
To verify effectiveness of implemented activities, the Project cooperated with the NFA on testing the beneficiary beekeepers honey samples for unauthorized residues within the National Honey Monitoring Program, being implemented by the NFA since 2014 by testing 100 samples annually. The Monitoring Program results have been showing positive trend of improving safety of Georgian honey. Rate of contaminated honey dropped from 54% in 2018 to 4% in 2021 and 2% in 2022.
The project has entered in post completion mode from October 2022 until December 31, 2023.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
